remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence was added; the Actor narrowed and caveated the same evidence rather than proving the missing predicate.

The policy threshold is rejection based on a material unresolved risk at the time of decision, and the available summary still does not independently show materiality or unresolved status at award time.
The cited procurement note, as summarized, supports follow-up or conditional approval if unresolved more clearly than it supports outright rejection.
The Actor's concessions reinforce that BPROC-002-C and BPROC-002-D alone point more naturally to follow-up or escalation than to reject-level action.

Because evidence access is limited to the Actor's summary, there is still no independent confirmation that follow-up was insufficient and rejection was policy-supported rather than merely conservative.
final_rationale: The audit picture did not materially change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record into a narrower argument: that rejection can be defended only as a conservative unresolved-risk decision and not as proof of a confirmed control failure. That narrowing is useful, but it does not cure the core compliance gap identified in the initial report. Under the policy text, rejection must rest on admissible evidence of a material unresolved risk at the time of decision. Based on the available summary alone, the record still shows questionnaire/storage inconsistency, an informal quality process, and a procurement follow-up note; those facts support diligence concern, follow-up, or escalation more clearly than they establish a reject-level threshold. This is the key distinction: a caveated framing can make an overbroad claim less problematic, but it is not enough for compliant_with_caveats when the caveat itself depends on an unresolved factual predicate that the admissible record has not been shown to satisfy. Accordingly, the claim remains suspicious rather than compliant.
